sermons.life_context: He was directing the orphan work at Ashley Down, Bristol. By his own count in these addresses he then oversaw three orphan houses and six schools, and two more houses opened by 1870. He also kept preaching in Bristol, where Henry Craik remained his co-worker until Craik died in 1866.

He was directing the Ashley Down orphan houses in Bristol. Three months earlier, on 22 January 1866, Henry Craik, his co-worker in Bristol since 1832, had died after a seven-month illness. Müller's own record calls Craik his intimate friend of thirty-six years.

He was directing the Ashley Down orphan houses in Bristol. Mary, his wife since October 1830, died on 6 February 1870, a month after New Orphan House No. 5 opened and completed room for about 2,000 orphans.

He was preaching in Bristol and directing the Ashley Down orphan houses, sharing direction with James Wright since May 1872. He had been widowed in 1870, and in November 1871 he married Susannah Grace Sangar, two weeks after his daughter Lydia married Wright.

He was back in Bristol after the first of his preaching tours, on which his second wife Susannah had set out with him on 26 March 1875. His son-in-law James Wright had shared direction of the orphan work since May 1872.

He was in Bristol between preaching tours, on which his wife Susannah travelled with him. His son-in-law James Wright, who had shared direction of the orphan work since May 1872, carried much of that work in Bristol.

He had been based in Bristol since his last preaching tour ended in May 1892. There he worked mainly for the Scriptural Knowledge Institution with his son-in-law James Wright and preached at Bethesda and elsewhere. His daughter Lydia had died in 1890, and his second wife Susannah in January 1895 (some sources give 1894).

His touring had ended in May 1892, and in these final Bristol years he worked mainly for the Scriptural Knowledge Institution with James Wright. He preached at Bethesda Chapel and elsewhere. He had been widowed twice, in February 1870 and in January 1895 (some sources say 1894), and his daughter Lydia had died in 1890.

He had been back in Bristol since his tours ended in May 1892. He worked mainly for the Scriptural Knowledge Institution with James Wright and preached at Bethesda Chapel and elsewhere. He had outlived his first wife Mary (died 1870), his daughter Lydia (died 1890) and his second wife Susannah (died January 1895; some sources say 1894).

He had been based in Bristol since his last tour ended in May 1892, preaching at Bethesda, where he had ministered since 1832. He had outlived Mary (died 1870), his daughter Lydia (died 1890) and Susannah (died January 1895; some sources say 1894). He died at Ashley Down about five months later, on 10 March 1898.
